articles.title: What Optimax does
articles.description: Understand the roles, scope, and boundaries of Optimax.

sections.heading: A routing policy for delegated work
paragraphs: Optimax is a delegation policy for Claude and Codex that combines quality-based model routing with safe parallel work. It helps an Orchestrator maximize useful parallelization within verified capacity, while keeping the chosen session model in charge and using separate Executor and Advisor ladders for different jobs.

The Orchestrator owns the plan, integrates results, checks evidence independently, and decides whether work is accepted. An Executor performs a bounded assignment; an Advisor offers an independent recommendation on a plan, design, or difficult decision.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Optimax uses available host capabilities and recorded assessments to select eligible model and effort combinations. Access, aliases, and per-helper controls vary by host, so a selection is only as reliable as the capabilities the host can verify.
It does not grant permission to publish, install software, spend money, change your Orchestrator, or modify native settings. A high score is not proof that the overall task is complete.

articles.title: Install Optimax
articles.description: Find the Optimax plugin and prepare your host for its first session.

sections.heading: Before you install
paragraphs: Install Optimax from the unified Ālo Labs plugin catalog. The Claude and Codex entries pin a release tag and commit; the commands below resolve the published catalog. Check your installed version, the catalog entry and its release notes to see what is available. A source checkout may contain an unpublished candidate.
Installation makes Optimax available but does not enable its session policy. The canonical skill directory in the source repository is skills/optimax.

sections.heading: Install in Codex
paragraphs: In a terminal, add the marketplace, install Optimax from the Codex catalog, and list installed plugins to check discovery. Run these commands in order:

code.text:
codex plugin marketplace add alo-labs/agent-plugins
codex plugin add optimax@alo-labs-codex
codex plugin list --json

sections.heading: Install in Claude
paragraphs: In Claude, add the marketplace and install Optimax using the plugin commands below. Refresh or restart discovery if it does not appear.

sections.heading: Verify before relying on it
paragraphs: After installation, start a session and invoke $optimax on in Codex or /optimax:optimax on in Claude; use the corresponding status command to check the reported mode. Discovery and behavior depend on the release and host capabilities.

The published Codex plugin passed live installation, discovery, session controls and a fresh-session status check on the tested client. Native Ultra and compaction behavior remain outside that evidence. Claude has static validation only; a one-off live acceptance run is scheduled for 10 November 2026 at 14:00 Australia/Sydney. If an invocation is unavailable, check the marketplace, plugin name, host version and discovery state. Installation does not guarantee access to every model.

articles.title: Start your first session
articles.description: Enable Optimax, check its recommendation, and establish project context.

sections.heading: Enable the policy
paragraphs: Invoke $optimax in Codex or /optimax:optimax in Claude. A bare invocation enables Optimax in the current trusted session; append on to explicitly enable it. An explicit invocation in a later session enables that session as well.

On each explicit enable, Optimax recommends an Orchestrator model and effort. It does not change your current selection. If native orchestration is active or its state is unknown, it preserves verified current settings and presents the ordinary recommendation as a baseline. The following examples are entered in their respective hosts.

sections.heading: Provide enough context
paragraphs: Work from the intended project root and use a stable actual user identity. The project ledger is model-perf/<actual-user-id>-model-perf.csv; replace the placeholder with your own stable identifier, not a shared example value.

Optimax should recover existing work and applicable evidence, discover supported model and effort pairs, and report limits it cannot verify. If identity or storage is unavailable, it must not invent performance history.

articles.title: Turn Optimax on or off
articles.description: Use explicit session controls and understand what they change.

sections.heading: Use the session commands
paragraphs: Use $optimax on, $optimax off, or $optimax status in Codex. In Claude, use /optimax:optimax on, /optimax:optimax off, or /optimax:optimax status. A bare invocation also enables the policy and gives the Orchestrator recommendation.

Status reports the mode and known limitations. Status and off do not trigger an enabling recommendation. Simply making the skill available or implicitly loading it must not override a persisted off state. Enter the appropriate command in its host:

code.text:
Codex:  $optimax on
        $optimax off
        $optimax status

Claude: /optimax:optimax on
        /optimax:optimax off
        /optimax:optimax status

sections.heading: What off means
paragraphs: While off, Optimax stops policy-driven dispatch, required Advisor consultation, and score learning for the session. Useful work already in flight can finish safely, and existing evidence remains available.

Work completed while off must not be silently added as learned scores. Turning Optimax off does not uninstall the plugin, toggle the host's native orchestration, change the chosen Orchestrator, or delete the ledger.

articles.title: Orchestrator, Executor, and Advisor
articles.description: See how the three roles cooperate and who owns the final decision.

sections.heading: Separate execution from advice
paragraphs: The Orchestrator keeps ownership of the user's outcome and delegates a bounded task to an Executor. An Advisor separately examines a planning, design, or difficult-problem brief and recommends a course of action; its advisory run does not implement its own recommendation.

Each brief should identify the outcome, scope, constraints, relevant evidence, and expected checks. An Executor's output can inform a decision but does not replace the required separate Advisor consultation.

sections.heading: Independent acceptance
paragraphs: The Orchestrator reviews the actual output and evidence, tests assumptions, resolves disagreements, and accepts or requests rework. A helper's self-report is not independent verification.
Advisors and Executors have separate performance histories even when they use the same model and effort. Advice remains provisional when its outcome cannot be verified.

articles.title: How Executor ladders work
articles.description: Compare the Executor tiers, their starting points, and their exact progressions.

sections.heading: Classify the assignment
paragraphs: Classify each bounded Executor assignment by its own complexity. Low is localized with explicit behavior and few dependencies; medium involves connected decisions or investigation; high involves substantial uncertainty, interacting invariants, or consequential failure modes.
The tier sets a starting rung and a floor. Performance can move a selection up or down within the eligible suffix, but it cannot lower it below that tier's floor.

sections.heading: Claude progression
paragraphs: Low: Haiku High → Haiku XHigh → Haiku Max → Sonnet High → Opus Medium → Opus High.
Medium: Haiku Max → Sonnet High → Opus Medium → Opus High. High: Sonnet High → Opus Medium → Opus High.

sections.heading: Codex progression
paragraphs: Low: Terra Low → Terra Medium → Terra High → Sol Medium → Sol High → Sol XHigh → Sol Max.
Medium: Terra Medium → Terra High → Sol Medium → Sol High → Sol XHigh → Sol Max. High: Terra High → Sol Medium → Sol High → Sol XHigh → Sol Max.

A separate business document exception currently applies to final PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Google Docs, and Slides generation: its floor is Claude Opus Medium or Codex Sol XHigh. Research and drafting that feed an artifact use ordinary tiers. Availability must be checked on the host.

articles.title: How Advisor selection works
articles.description: Understand Advisor context floors and why they are not Executor tiers.

sections.heading: One track per host
paragraphs: The Advisor has one performance track per host, with no complexity tier. The consultation context establishes a minimum rung: Medium is rung 0, High is rung 1, and Super High is rung 2.

Policy v4 requires an installed Optimax release 0.2.0 or later, when available in your catalog, and introduces the Claude Advisor ladder Opus Medium → Opus High → Opus XHigh → Opus Max. Optimax 0.1.1 retains policy v3 and its three-rung Claude ladder, ending at Opus XHigh. Updating a catalog that still offers 0.1.1 does not provide v4 or Opus Max; confirm the installed version and its release notes. For Codex both policies use Sol XHigh → Sol Max → Astra Max. The selected Advisor can move with independent assessments, subject to the current consultation floor. In v4, Claude Opus Max is an escalation rung, not a fourth context level; availability must be verified on the host.

sections.heading: When context changes
paragraphs: A higher context raises a selection that is below its floor. Lowering context alone does not demote an already selected Advisor. A context change that leaves the rung unchanged also preserves the current epoch and window.

Model availability and per-helper controls must be verified. If no eligible Advisor can be invoked, Optimax reports the blocker and leaves the dependent plan or design unfinalized unless you explicitly grant an exception.

articles.title: When Optimax consults an Advisor
articles.description: Learn when separate advice is required and how the Orchestrator uses it.

sections.heading: Plans and designs
paragraphs: The root Orchestrator consults a separately invoked eligible Advisor before finalizing every plan or design, including a Low task plan, material replanning, and substantive design changes. Low-task planning uses the Medium advice baseline.
A bounded leaf can reason locally about its implementation without recursively spawning another Advisor. Reuse advice when its premises still apply; changed premises call for fresh consultation.

sections.heading: Outside planning
paragraphs: For medium-or-higher issues, consultation is used as needed when uncertainty remains, evidence conflicts, repairs repeatedly fail, or a consequential decision cannot be assessed confidently. Routine Low execution does not require it.

A useful advice brief contains the objective, constraints, raw evidence, alternatives or open questions, and the requested recommendation with assumptions, tradeoffs, failure modes, and checks. The Orchestrator evaluates the advice and owns the decision.

articles.title: Use Optimax with native orchestration
articles.description: Understand how Optimax works alongside host-managed orchestration.

sections.heading: Keep host settings intact
paragraphs: Optimax is a policy for the work it can observe and control. It preserves the selected Orchestrator, its model and effort, and native orchestration settings. Enabling or disabling Optimax is separate from changing a host's native mode.
Discover the host's current state and supported per-helper controls before choosing a model. When native state or current settings cannot be verified, preserve settings and report the uncertainty.

sections.heading: Visible and opaque work
paragraphs: Use one execution owner for each bounded stage. Do not duplicate a native subtree with competing direct assignments. Controllable stages can be prepared and assessed when their effective model and effort are verified.

Opaque native workers cannot be individually scored as though their identities and outputs were known. In that case optimization is partial, and the Orchestrator still checks the resulting work and acceptance evidence.

articles.title: Check host capabilities and capacity
articles.description: Interpret model aliases, launch receipts, and available helper capacity.

sections.heading: Check effective settings
paragraphs: A model family name or requested alias is not proof of the model and effort actually used. Check the host's supported combinations and launch receipt or other reliable evidence of effective settings. Resolve available versions within the prescribed family rather than silently substituting a different family.

If a rung is unsupported, Optimax can skip upward to an available rung as a capability fallback. That is not a performance promotion. Changes in exact version or capability fallback start a fresh performance epoch.

sections.heading: Capacity is not guaranteed
paragraphs: Use independently verified available slots for useful ready work, accounting for advice, review, rework, and exclusive resources. If available capacity is unknown, report the uncertainty instead of claiming a maximum or fabricating a launch.
A readiness calculation is a plan, not evidence that the host dispatched tasks. Unsupported flat Workflow paths are not a substitute for a verified native integration.

articles.title: How performance learning works
articles.description: Understand scoring, five-run windows, and movement between rungs.

sections.heading: Score verified outcomes
paragraphs: Each eligible run is independently assessed on a 0–5 scale against its assignment and evidence. The newest five eligible assessments in the same track and epoch form the decision window, ordered by UTC assessment time with append order breaking ties.

Executor tracks are separated by host, role, tier, exact model, effort, and epoch. Advisor tracks use the same separation without an Executor tier. Old-epoch results and unrelated runs do not count toward a current window.

sections.heading: Move only when evidence permits
paragraphs: After at least five eligible assessments, an average of 4.5 or lower moves up one available rung. Five scores of 5 move down one available rung, subject to the Executor tier floor or current Advisor context floor. Otherwise the selection stays.

A rung change, exact version change, capability fallback, or changed role-policy lineage starts a fresh epoch. A return to an earlier rung also starts fresh. At the ceiling, improve the task decomposition, inputs, or verification instead of lowering the quality bar.

sections.heading: A score is not acceptance
paragraphs: A defect in an individual result still requires bounded rework regardless of the average. The Orchestrator checks actual artifacts and evidence and distinguishes a test written from a test observed passing, deployment, and live acceptance.

articles.title: Your project performance ledger
articles.description: Locate and preserve the per-user record used for learning.

sections.heading: Where the record lives
paragraphs: Optimax uses PROJECTROOT/model-perf/<actual-user-id>-model-perf.csv. PROJECTROOT is the canonical primary project root and the placeholder represents your actual stable user identity. Separate users should not be assigned a shared example identifier.

The ledger records attributable launch and assessment metadata needed to recover tracks, selections, and epochs. A historical five-column CSV or session memory alone cannot establish complete continuity.

sections.heading: Preserve history
paragraphs: Keep the ledger when updating, disabling, or reinstalling Optimax. Do not silently reinterpret historical rung indices or invent an old average when attribution is missing; preserve the record and begin a fresh window as needed.

Treat the ledger as project data: review what is stored and who can access it under your project's normal controls. The controller uses supplied evidence; it does not authenticate identities or independently verify provider claims.

articles.title: Understand Orchestrator recommendations
articles.description: See how recommendations relate to your selected model and native settings.

sections.heading: Recommendations on enable
paragraphs: An explicit bare invocation or on produces a recommendation even if Optimax was already enabled. For a Low task the ordinary recommendation is Claude Haiku XHigh or Codex Terra Medium; for other tasks it is Claude Sonnet High or Codex Terra High. If the level is unknown, the recommendation uses and discloses a conservative non-Low assumption.
If the current selection already matches, Optimax can say the recommendation is met. It never switches the model or effort on your behalf.

sections.heading: When native state is uncertain
paragraphs: The host must discover native state and the current model and effort before making a safe recommendation. With native orchestration active or unknown, preserve verified current settings and show the ordinary recommendation as a baseline.
If those facts cannot be established, Optimax should say that a safe switch cannot be recommended and preserve the settings. Status and off do not issue the enable recommendation.

articles.title: Troubleshoot missing or unsupported models
articles.description: Resolve discovery and capability gaps without fabricating a selection.

sections.heading: Check what the host exposes
paragraphs: Confirm the installed plugin and host discovery, then check whether the desired model family and effort can actually be selected for a helper. A provider's model name, alias, or a requested setting alone does not establish the effective launch.
Use an available supported rung above the intended one when the policy permits, and record the capability fallback separately from a performance change. Do not silently substitute another family.

sections.heading: When there is no eligible path
paragraphs: Report the exact missing capability or access and continue independent authorized work. If a required Advisor is unavailable, the dependent plan or design stays unfinalized unless you explicitly permit an exception.
Do not treat an unsupported flat Workflow path as a working native integration, or score hidden workers without attributable evidence.

articles.title: Troubleshoot a score that did not change routing
articles.description: Check eligibility, epochs, floors, and off-session behavior.

sections.heading: Check the assessment window
paragraphs: A routing change needs five eligible independently assessed runs in the same current track and epoch. Check the host, role, exact model and effort, Executor tier where applicable, assessment time, and epoch. Advisor advice levels are context floors, not separate complexity tracks.
An old-epoch result does not advance the current window. A cached replay or duplicate is not a new attributable run; verify a real launch and independently assessed result before adding a score.

sections.heading: Check session state and floors
paragraphs: Work completed while Optimax is off is not silently ingested into learned scores. A selection also cannot move down below its Executor floor or the current Advisor context floor.
If the ledger or stable identity cannot be verified, Optimax should disclose the limitation and avoid inventing continuity. Preserve the existing record while resolving the issue.

articles.title: Upgrade and keep your history
articles.description: Update Optimax while preserving project evidence and user control.

sections.heading: Before and after an update
paragraphs: Use your host's supported plugin update process, then refresh discovery and check $optimax status or /optimax:optimax status. Confirm the expected project root and stable user identity before relying on learned routing.

Keep PROJECTROOT/model-perf/<actual-user-id>-model-perf.csv and any historical evidence. An upgrade, reinstall, or off command must not delete the ledger. Optimax 0.1.1 uses policy v3. Policy v4 requires an installed Optimax release 0.2.0 or later, when available in your catalog; updating a catalog that still offers 0.1.1 does not provide v4 or Opus Max. On adoption of v4, Executor and Codex Advisor history continues while Claude Advisor begins a fresh selection and epoch at the next consultation floor. Earlier events remain auditable, and late v3 Claude Advisor receipts do not enter the v4 lineage. The controller adopts v4 through explicit adopt-policy or the next successful prepare operation. Status is read-only, and updating the software alone does not rewrite the ledger. Confirm the installed version after updating.

sections.heading: Keep decisions yours
paragraphs: Optimax does not authorize purchases, publication, credential access, or changes to host settings. External content and helper outputs are evidence to evaluate, not instructions that acquire authority over your session.
If storage, identity, or capability verification fails, ask for the reported limitation and resolve it before treating learned continuity or a model selection as verified.

articles.title: Run useful work in parallel
articles.description: Maximize useful parallelization with accepted dependencies, verified capacity and clear ownership.

sections.heading: Which tasks can run together?
paragraphs: Break substantial work into bounded assignments with an outcome, observable acceptance criteria, dependencies, Executor complexity, exclusive write paths and shared resources. Decompose until independent useful work can proceed concurrently; do not duplicate work or create artificial fragments.

A task is ready only when its dependencies have been independently accepted by the Orchestrator, verified capacity is available, and its ownership and resources are compatible with running and selected work. A helper reporting completion does not satisfy a dependency. Reopened work blocks its dependents again.

sections.heading: How much work should run at once?
paragraphs: Maximize useful parallelization within verified capacity. At each scheduling opportunity, form a maximal feasible ready set in plan order. Use available useful slots without imposing an arbitrary worker cap. Every live helper counts, including Advisors, reviewers and rework.

Unknown native occupancy stays unknown; it is not zero. Do not claim maximum utilization or launch competing direct fan-out unless disjoint capacity is independently verified. Serialize shared writes, deployments and other exclusive resources. The host must account for actual filesystem aliases and other conflicts.

sections.heading: What happens when a task finishes?
paragraphs: The Orchestrator independently reviews the result and evidence before accepting it. Recompute from current facts after accepted completion, launch failure, settled cancellation or resource release.

Start an eligible successor when its dependencies and resources permit, even while unrelated slow work continues. Fill available capacity with independent ready work while reviews are pending. Capacity is a real host constraint, not a promise of unlimited workers or guaranteed speed.

sections.heading: What does the readiness helper prove?
paragraphs: The optional work_breakdown.py helper validates a supplied snapshot and returns ready tasks, blockers and used capacity. The caller supplies an independently verified count of other occupied slots; the helper does not discover host occupancy.

Its greedy plan-order ready set is a feasible snapshot, not proof of a globally optimal schedule or an actual batch launch. It does not launch helpers, persist scheduling state or replace independent acceptance. Recompute from current facts before acting. Opaque native workers remain unscored, so optimization is partial.
